The results show a critically low CD4 count of 36/mm3, placing you at extreme risk for opportunistic infections, while the normal angiography rules out vascular causes. Given your visual symptoms and immunosuppression, we must urgently investigate for CMV retinitis, which often presents with peripheral vision loss before the center, and potentially syphilis. Do you have any recent history of syphilis, and can you describe if your vision loss is central or affecting your peripheral field?

REQUEST TEST: Syphilis serology (RPR/FTA-ABS) and OCT of the right eye.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages are pathognomonic for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, even though the earlier angiography was normal. Given your critically low CD4 count of 36/mm3, this is consistent with your severe immunosuppression.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis
